___ prior to her CABG. Because the pain was similar she 
decided to come to the ED. Pain does not worsen with exertion. 
She had no associated diaphoresis, nausea, or vomitting. Of

1. Coronary angiography of this right dominant system 
demonstrated 3 vessel coronary artery disease. The LMCA had mild 
distal disease. The LAD was diffusely diseased with subtotal

proximal stenosis and complete occlusion immediately after a 
large OM1. There was no collateral filling of the distal LCx. 
The RCA was a small vessel with a high rising, short, small PDA. 
The RCA had diffuse disease with less than 50% stenoses.

calculated LVEF was 72%. There was a small segment of 
inferobasilar  
akinesis and the apex tip was akinetic. The remainder of the LV 
was  
hyperkinetic.

1. Three vessel coronary artery disease.  
2. Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction.  
3. Regional left ventricular wall motion abnormality.

___ 03:15PM   PLT COUNT-___ year old female with history of CAD s/p NSTEMI and CABG 
(___), hypothyroidism, hyperlipidemia who presented with left 
arm pain which is cocerning for her anginal equivalent.  
.  
#. CAD: Pt has known CAD with prior CABG and presented with arm 
pain that is reportedly her anginal equivalent. ETT was 
performed and was nondiagnostic. CE were negative. Cardiac Cath 
was performed and revealed a 90% discrete lesion in the AV 
groove LCX that was ungrafted and supplied a distal OM.  POBA 
without stenting was performed and TIMI 3 flow and 10% residual 
was achieved.  Patient was discharged on ASA 325 mg and 
increased dose of Metoprolol Tartrate of 50 mg daily.
.  
#. Pump: nml EF on last echo, no clinical evidence of failure 
and no evidence of failure on CXR. 1+ edema is chronic and 
likely due to venous insufficiency after SVG harvesting.
.  
#. Rhythm: Normal sinus rhythm.  
.  
#. Hyperlipidemia: continued atorvastatin 80 mg daily.  
.  
#. Anxiety: pt reported symptoms of anxiety. She sees an 
acupuntcturist. She is not currently on and SSRI.  Did not start 
SSRI given acute CAD, but would recomend starting it as an 
outpatient.  
.  
#. Hypothyroidism: Continued on outpatient levothyroxine.

patient had left arm pain lasting roughly ___ minutes following 
the catheterization and pain resolved on its own.  It is 
unlikely that this pain is due to cardiac ischemia.

 
Discharge Instructions:
you were admitted to the hospital with left arm pain.  Because 
this pain was similar to the pain you had prior to your 
myocardial infarction you were admitted.  Blood tests showed 
that you did not have a myocardial infarction.  You have a 
cardiac catheterization that showed narrowing of one of the 
small arteries of the heart.  An angioplasty was performed to 
open this vessel, but no stent was placed.  It is most likely 
that your arm pain is not related to heart disease.  
.
Your Toprol dose was increased and you should take a full dose 
aspirin (325 mg) daily.
.

.

below.
